# package testutil

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-sunspec/testutil"
```

Package testutil provides an in-process SunSpec Modbus TCP fixture for tests: a register map builder, a read-only request handler serving it, and a helper that starts a server with a connected client.

## Functions

### func StartServerClient

```go
func StartServerClient(t *testing.T, handler *SunSpecHandler, port int) (*modbus.Client, func())
```

StartServerClient creates a test server/client pair. Returns cleanup function.

The server listens on tcp://127.0.0.1:\<port> and accepts up to two clients, one of which is the returned, already opened client. Any failure to start the server or connect fails the test immediately with t.Fatalf. The caller must call the cleanup function, which closes the client and stops the server; calling it more than once is harmless.

### func StringToRegisters

```go
func StringToRegisters(s string, regCount int) []uint16
```

StringToRegisters encodes a string into big-endian registers, padded with NULs.

The result always has regCount registers: s is truncated to regCount\*2 bytes when it is longer. This is the SunSpec "string" point encoding.

## Types

### type FixtureModel

```go
type FixtureModel struct {
	// ID is the SunSpec model ID written to the model header.
	ID uint16
	// Length is the model length written to the model header: the number of
	// data registers, excluding the two header registers. The next model
	// header is placed Length registers after this model's data starts.
	Length uint16
	// Registers holds the data registers that follow the header. It may be
	// shorter than Length, which leaves the remaining addresses unmapped so
	// that reading them fails with an illegal data address exception.
	Registers []uint16
}
```

FixtureModel defines one model's register data for a test fixture.

### type SunSpecHandler

```go
type SunSpecHandler struct {
	// Registers maps a zero-based register address to its value. Reading an
	// address that is not in the map fails with modbus.ErrIllegalDataAddress.
	Registers map[uint16]uint16
	// UnitID is the only Modbus unit ID the handler answers.
	UnitID uint8
}
```

SunSpecHandler implements modbus.RequestHandler for testing. It serves holding register reads from a sparse register map and rejects everything else.

The handler does not lock Registers: populate the map before the server starts and do not modify it while requests may be served.

#### func NewSunSpecFixture

```go
func NewSunSpecFixture(baseAddr uint16, unitID uint8, models ...FixtureModel) *SunSpecHandler
```

NewSunSpecFixture builds a register map with SunSpec marker, model headers, and data.

The "SunS" marker is written at baseAddr, followed by each model (header, then data) in the given order and the end-of-chain marker (0xFFFF, 0). The returned handler answers only unitID. Addresses are not checked for overflow of the 16-bit address space.

#### func (SunSpecHandler) HandleCoils

```go
func (h *SunSpecHandler) HandleCoils(_ context.Context, _ *modbus.CoilsRequest) ([]bool, error)
```

HandleCoils rejects every coil request with modbus.ErrIllegalFunction.

#### func (SunSpecHandler) HandleDiscreteInputs

```go
func (h *SunSpecHandler) HandleDiscreteInputs(_ context.Context, _ *modbus.DiscreteInputsRequest) ([]bool, error)
```

HandleDiscreteInputs rejects every discrete input request with modbus.ErrIllegalFunction.

#### func (SunSpecHandler) HandleHoldingRegisters

```go
func (h *SunSpecHandler) HandleHoldingRegisters(_ context.Context, req *modbus.HoldingRegistersRequest) ([]uint16, error)
```

HandleHoldingRegisters serves holding register reads from Registers.

It returns modbus.ErrIllegalFunction for a write or for a unit ID other than UnitID, and modbus.ErrIllegalDataAddress when any requested address is not in Registers.

#### func (SunSpecHandler) HandleInputRegisters

```go
func (h *SunSpecHandler) HandleInputRegisters(_ context.Context, _ *modbus.InputRegistersRequest) ([]uint16, error)
```

HandleInputRegisters rejects every input register request with modbus.ErrIllegalFunction.
